compliance.emc: FCC 47 CFR Part 15; ICES-003; BS EN 55032; BS EN 55035; EN 300 386; CISPR 32; CISPR 35; IEC/EN 61000 series (guide, Compliance Statements for EMC Requirements)
compliance.nebs: designed to comply with Zone 4 earthquake requirements of NEBS GR-63-CORE, Issue 3 (guide Table 24)

environmental.altitude: no performance degradation to 1828.8 m (6000 ft) at 0 to 40 C for AFO; for AFI the figure is 0 ft (guide Table 24)
environmental.operating-temp: 0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F) for AFO and AFI (guide Table 24)
environmental.storage-temp: -40 to 70 C (-40 to 158 F) in the shipping container

features.optics-qsfp-dd: 400 GbE QSFP-DD optics; 400G-ZR and 400G-ZRM only in ports 33 to 63 (the odd ones of the lower band)

performance.breakout-ports: up to 64 x 400 GbE, 128 x 200 GbE, 256 x 100 GbE, 256 x 40 GbE, 256 x 25 GbE or 256 x 10 GbE (guide, QFX5230-64CD Switch Description)
performance.qsfpdd-speeds: 400, 200, 100, 50, 40 GbE, 4 x 25 GbE or 4 x 10 GbE per port (guide, Port Panel overview)

physical.weight-note: 55 lb (25 kg) with power supplies and fans installed (guide Table 8)

power.power-input-dc: rated -48 to -60 VDC, operating -40 to -72 VDC (guide Table 18)
power.power-measurement-note: Maximum at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic; typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load with IMIX traffic, excluding transceivers (guide Table 13)
power.redundancy-note: two supplies, 1+1, hot-removable and hot-insertable while the second supply is installed

thermal.airflow-note: AFO is front-to-back (port-to-FRU); AFI is back-to-front (FRU-to-port); no mixing of fans and supplies of different direction
thermal.fans: four fan modules of two rotors, 7+1 at rotor level; the switch runs 120 seconds without thermal shutdown while one module is replaced

configs.description: QFX5230-64CD-AFI: two 2700 W AC supplies (JNP-2700W-AC-AFI) and four back-to-front fan modules (QFX5230-64CD-FANAI). All have a green handle and the label AIR IN (guide Tables 3 and 6).
configs.name: ac-b2f

configs.description: QFX5230-64CD-AFO: two 3000 W AC supplies (JNP-3000W-AC-AFO) and four front-to-back fan modules (QFX5230-64CD-FANAO). All have a Juniper gold handle and the label AIR OUT (guide Tables 3 and 6).
configs.name: ac-f2b

configs.description: QFX5230-64CD-CHAS, the spare chassis, shipped without power supplies or fan modules ("Spare Chassis without PSU and Fans"). Either AC or DC supplies and AIR OUT or AIR IN fan modules are ordered separately, and supplies and fans of one airflow only go in. The supply and fan bays are shown open.
configs.name: chas

configs.description: QFX5230-64CD-D-AFI: two 2400 W DC supplies (JNP-2400W-DC-AFI) and four back-to-front fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.
configs.name: dc-b2f

configs.description: QFX5230-64CD-D-AFO: two 3000 W DC supplies (JNP-3000W-DC-AFO) and four front-to-back fan modules. Each supply has a single feed, so feeds A and B go one to each.
configs.name: dc-f2b

gaps.wanted: The rear panel's own colour. The photograph shows a dark grey rear (#595a61) behind a silver front (#dbdcde); the format has one chassis colour, so the rear is drawn in the front's silver.
The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures 15, 20 and 22 carry no scale and its tables state weights only for the whole chassis.

A photograph or flat figure of the DC supply (the guide's figure 22 is an isometric), of the AIR IN supplies and of the AIR IN fan module. Their faces are drawn from the AIR OUT AC art with the guide's handle colour and label and are estimated.

The DC models' power figures. Guide Table 17, headed DC, prints 487 W typical and 1446 W maximum at 220-240 V followed by "(AC)". They are carried as the DC models' figures; whether they are AC input figures for the DC models is not stated.

The rated input of the AFO DC 3000 W supply. Guide Table 18 prints "50-60 Hz" in the rated column for it, where the AFI row prints -48 to -60 VDC; the supply is a DC unit (-40 to -72 VDC), so -48 to -60 VDC is carried.

The protective earthing terminal. The guide's figure 8 and Ground the QFX5230-64CD Switch (two 10-32 screws with the lug's posts pointing right) show it on the side of the chassis, which no figure draws flat and no photograph shows. It is not drawn.

The lamps of the RJ-45 jacks. The guide's management panel lists the three chassis lamps and the network lamps only (figure 14, Table 10); the photograph shows lamp windows at the corners of the management jack. The management jack is drawn with the library's lamped jack and the console jack bare.

The connector type of the 10M and PPS jacks. The guide calls them "SMB" connectors in the specification list and "clock input and output connectors" in figure 12; the photograph shows gold coaxial jacks 6 mm across, drawn as the library's SMA jack. Estimated.
The rating label printed on each supply (an AC input line, a DC input line) and the guide's serial number labels (figures 55 to 58). Not drawn.
The short dash after each port numeral on the metal, which points at the cage. Not drawn: the numerals are drawn alone.
The rack ears' positions and the rack kits' contracts. The guide names rack kits only in its inventory and its installation figures; no kit contract exists in the library and none is written here.

chassis.note: guide Table 8: 3.43 in (8.7 cm) high, 17.4 in (44.2 cm) wide, 25.6 in (65 cm) deep, 55 lb (25 kg) with power supplies and fans installed, 2RU. The inch figures are used and the centimetre ones in the same cell are rounded copies of them. The table does not say whether the width is over the brackets: the guide's rack figures show brackets bolted to the sides and the photographs show a body 4.150 px/mm wide with no brackets, so the width is the body and brackets are not modelled. The table does not say whether the depth includes the handles of the supplies and fans.

colour.note: The front plate samples #dbdcde (median of a bare patch between two cages) and the rear panel #595a61. The chassis colour is the front's, because a device has one colour for every face; the rear is therefore drawn light where the real rear is dark grey, and its legends are drawn dark to stay readable on that. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

drawing-vs-photo.note: The guide's figure 10 is the same studio photograph at reduced size, the AIR OUT AC build with orange handles, and the photograph agrees with it. The guide shows no AIR IN, DC or empty-bay rear, and no photograph of one is held, so those configurations are drawn from the component art.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide's installation figures 1 to 7 (side mounting brackets, mounting rails, front and rear rails) and its switch-tray assembly (figures 25 to 37, Tables 37 to 40, an Open Rack v3 mounting) are kit procedures. The guide gives the kit part numbers only in its sample inventory (Table 36). The library holds no contract for either kit and none is written here, so `chassis.ears` and `chassis.kits` are left out and a gap says so. The modelled body is the 441.96 mm chassis, without brackets.

front-green-tab.note: The green tab at the right edge, 3.8 mm wide and 17.1 mm tall, is the serial-number pull-out. It is drawn as decor, because it is a label card and not a part the library models. Guide figure 12 shows no callout for it on the QFX5230.

gate-1.note: The front photograph's body, between the left and right edges, is 1834 px wide and 361 px from the top edge to the bottom lip, an aspect of 5.08 against the table's 441.96 / 87.12 = 5.07 (0.2 percent out, so the photograph is near-orthographic). Scale 4.150 px/mm across, used on both axes with the origin at the left edge (x 123 px) and the top edge (y 169 px). The rear photograph's body is 1829 px wide, 4.138 px/mm. The guide's figures 9 to 13 are half-tone thumbnails and are used only to count and read.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. The guide, published 2026-04-28, states none and no Juniper notice was found in the intake. The device states none announced. Estimated, because absence in the guide is not a notice from the maker.

logo.note: The maker's logo and its lockup are printed at the upper right of the face, above the model name QFX5230-64CD. The logo is not drawn: a logo-zone region is reserved where it stands, and the model name is drawn as plain text.

mgmt-panel.note: Right of the last column, from the top: the RJ-45 management and console jacks side by side in one shield under the maker's logo, labelled MGMT and CON, the SFP+ pair with 64 and 65 above it, the three chassis lamps ALM, SYS and ID in a column with their legends below them and the green serial-number tab beside them, the 10M and PPS coaxial jacks, the round ESD point, the USB-A port with the reset hole and the model name. The jacks are turned a quarter turn, so the latch faces a side edge; which side is not seen and 90 is used. The shield is 23.9 mm wide and holds two jacks, 11.9 mm each; the library's jack is 13.2 mm across when turned, so the two are placed 13.4 mm apart and overhang the shield by 1.5 mm on the left (estimated). Guide figure 12 names the clock connectors "10MHz and 1PPS"; the metal prints 10M and PPS.

modules.note: The four fan modules (QFX5230-64CD-FANAO and -FANAI) and the two power supplies (JNP-3000W-AC-AFO, JNP-2700W-AC-AFI, JNP-3000W-DC-AFO and JNP-2400W-DC-AFI) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component. Table 6 names them with their handle colours. Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay. Each supply carries its own small fan inside (the cooling system is four fan modules of two rotors and a fan in each supply). The guide's figure 18 shows the fan module lamp but gives no place for it on the chassis, so it is not drawn.

port-lamps.note: Each QSFP-DD network port has a single bicolour lamp (guide, QFX5230-64CD Network LEDs, Table 9) on the left of its column: a round window 2.0 mm across at the height of its cage's centre, 2.8 mm left of the cell. The lamps are unlit in the photograph. The SFP+ ports show no lamp in the photograph and the guide describes none.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal beside each column, read off the photograph: each numeral is followed by a short dash that points at its cage (the dash is not drawn) and stands left of the column, the even number below a lamp for the upper cage and the odd number above a lamp for the lower one. The ports run 0 to 31 down each column and left to right in the upper band and 32 to 63 in the lower band; the SFP+ pair prints 64 above the upper cage and 65 above the lower one. The guide's figure 12 numbers the network ports as one group (callouts 1 and 2) and its note names ports 33 through 63. Interface names are not printed and none is stated in the guide's text held on this host, so they are not recorded.

ports.note: Front photograph: 64 QSFP-DD openings in two bands, each a row of 16 stacked pairs, the openings 78 px (18.8 mm) wide on a 104.5 px pitch, 25.19 mm. The cage cell is the registry's 19.0 mm, set so the opening centres agree; the first cell starts at 13.15 mm. Counts and the order are the guide's figures 9, 11 and 12 and the printed numerals. The two SFP+ cages stand to the right of the last column, one above the other, and are turned a quarter turn (callout 5 of figure 12; 10.3 mm wide and 15.3 mm tall in the photograph).

power.note: Table 13 (AC): 220 to 240 V, typical 498 W and maximum 1396 W. Table 17 (DC models): typical 487 W and maximum 1446 W, printed with "(AC)" after each figure although the table is headed DC; they are carried as the DC models' figures. Both tables say the maximum is measured at 40 C ambient with SR optics at 100 percent load with IMIX traffic and the typical at 25 C with DACs at 50 percent load, excluding transceivers. The AC pair is the device's, since AC is the default build; the DC pair is carried under its own keys. AC input 180 to 305 VAC at 50 or 60 Hz (Table 4); DC input -40 to -72 VDC, rated -48 to -60 VDC (Table 18).

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.138 px/mm, checked against the guide's figure 10: four fan modules numbered 0 to 3 from the left on an 86.7 mm pitch, then two supplies stacked at the right end, supply 0 above supply 1. A fan symbol and the module number are printed beside the lower left corner of each fan opening, and a power symbol with the supply number to the left of each supply. The fan frames measure 80.9 mm wide and 80.0 mm high; the supplies 74.8 mm wide and 40.2 mm high.

row-pitch.note: Down column 3 the four openings centre at 21.3, 36.9, 51.8 and 67.3 mm, so the rows are 15.5 mm apart inside a band (the registry gives no belly-to-belly pitch for a QSFP-DD cage) and the bands are 30.5 mm apart.

sources.note: QFX5230-64CD Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-04-28, 146 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2026), from https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/qfx5230/qfx5230.pdf: the front and rear figures 9 and 10, the port panel figures 11 to 14 and Tables 9 and 10 (lamps), Table 3 (hardware models), the cooling system (Tables 5, 6 and 11, figures 15 to 18), the power system (Tables 4, 12, 13, 16 to 22, figures 19 to 23) and Table 8 (physical specifications). The guide is Juniper's and public; its terms of use were not found in the document beyond the copyright notice and the end user licence agreement, so only facts are transcribed. Juniper's studio photographs of the 64CD, front and rear (qfx5230-64cd-front-high.jpg, 2100 x 710 px, and qfx5230-64cd-rear-high.jpg, 2100 x 765 px, from juniper.net's image library). No datasheet for the QFX5230 is held on the intake host (it is an HPE document, a00150804enw, listed in the intake notes as not fetched), no Visio stencil, no 3D model and no mechanical drawing was found in the intake folder or on juniper.net. The converted drawings of the guide are half-tone thumbnails: figures 9 and 10 are the same studio photographs at reduced size.

stack-orientation.note: The photograph shows the grey latch mesh between the two cages of every pair, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention. The convention is applied, not observed: the cages are dark openings in the photograph and the lip is not resolved.

variants.note: Table 3: QFX5230-64CD-AFO and -AFI (AC) and QFX5230-64CD-D-AFO and -D-AFI (DC), and the spare QFX5230-64CD-CHAS "Spare Chassis without PSU and Fans". All five share this front panel and the rear bays, so each is a configuration of this device. The handle colour of an AIR OUT module is Juniper gold and of an AIR IN module green, and the supplies of one airflow never mix with the fans of the other. The AIR IN AC supply is 2700 W and the AIR IN DC supply 2400 W; the AIR OUT supplies are 3000 W (Table 4).

vents.note: Hexagonal holes in the sheet: a band along the top above the cages (about 1.5 to 13 mm down), a band along the bottom (about 75 to 86 mm) and a column of holes left of the SFP+ pair. Drawn as vent decor in those positions, pitched to the photograph and estimated. Five dark slots at the left edge are the windows of the mounting ear and are drawn as dark decor; three round dimples at the right edge are not drawn.

zr-ports.note: The 16 ports marked in green, 33 to 63 (the odd numbers of the lower band), take 400G-ZR and 400G-ZRM optics and trigger an alarm if one goes in another port (figure 9 note). On the metal their numerals sit on a green chip, 3.5 mm wide and 2.5 mm tall in the photograph, drawn here as decor in the logo green, 3.8 by 2.6 mm, sampled from the photograph's serial-number tab.
